questions.question: Row identity for the sync: the outline says a node's row number is a slot reserved from the home librarian (CAIRN_HOME_HOST), with blanks the sync fills; the code keys a node by a content hash (trees.node_id_for, sha256 of the content) and the per-nexus tables are the leaf trees. Which stands for the sync: hash ids (the sync is a primary-key union, no reservation) or reserved integer slots?
questions.why: the sync's whole shape follows from it: with hashes a node is the same row on every box by construction and nothing needs reserving; with slots the librarian must hand out rows and the sync must hold blanks. The build assumes hashes (cairn_nodes node_id text PRIMARY KEY today).

questions.question: Direction: 11.3.5.1 says the remote syncs with the home box's database and that the sync is the backup. Is the sync home to remote only, or both ways (a node only the remote holds also goes to the home)?
questions.why: the build moves home to remote only; a both-ways sync needs the home to accept writes from a remote into tables its devices own

questions.question: Authority: the sync writes rows into tables that other devices own (librarian, codemother). May db_domain write for an owner by the registry's recorded owner, or must each owner opt its table in or run its own sync through the owner's gate?
questions.why: Law 6: the owner alone gates writes and delegation happens only through the owner's gate, never ambiently. The build takes an explicit `owners` set from its caller with no default, so nothing syncs for an owner nobody named, but who may name an owner is this question

questions.question: Conflict: when both boxes hold the same node or leaf id with different contents (a tree weight that moved on one box), who wins: the home, the newest, or neither (left and reported)?
questions.why: the build leaves the remote's row as it is and counts it as differing; learning weights are exactly the rows that will differ
